title: Quantum Time Crystal Ring: Period-Doubling Subharmonic Dynamics and Perturbation Tolerance on a 12-Qubit Superconducting Lattice Ring
description:
Preregistered experimental evaluation of discrete time crystalline (DTC) period-doubling dynamics and epsilon-tolerance in Floquet spin systems on an IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor (ibm_marrakesh, job dbuupiv82tmc73du4u70). Compares an unperturbed boundary-free 12-qubit regular ring (C12) against a 3-qubit triangle (C3) and non-interacting duration-matched controls (J=0). All 85 circuits executed under deterministic shuffle with count-level bootstrap analysis.

Key Findings:
- Primary Hypothesis P1 (Interaction Protection): SUPPORTED (Delta S(6) = +0.5527 [99% CI: 0.5385, 0.5671], p < 1e-5), demonstrating that many-body Ising interactions (J=0.4) stabilize period-doubling against single-qubit perturbation phase error (eps=0.10) where the non-interacting control rapidly collapses (S_J0 = 0.1163).
- Hypothesis P2 (Gumicsere / Inhomogeneity): Cyclic disorder permutations exhibit low variance (Var = 0.000076, sigma = 0.0087), indicating that physical qubit variation is averaged out across the closed ring topology.
- Hypothesis P3 (Epsilon Tolerance): Interacting period-doubling order persists across perturbations eps in [0.00, 0.10] (S_J = 0.6690).
- Triangle Module (N=3): The closed 3-qubit ring was heavily suppressed (S = 0.1917) compared to the open 3-qubit path (S = 0.6673). Because active SWAP routing requires 54 CZ gates on C3 versus 24 CZ on P3, gate infidelities and geometric frustration are confounded.
- Exploration Hypothesis: Measured contrast (+0.5527) is strictly bounded by hardware two-qubit gate noise, falling short of the noisy Aer model (+0.6605), confirming standard open quantum system Lindbladian decoherence.
